correctness.rationale: For real a, lambda > 0 the Gamma integral gives the coefficient with modulus Gamma(2a+1) t^(a+1/2) / [lambda^2(1+t)^2+y^2]^(a+1/2). The two norm squares contribute Gamma(2a+1)Gamma(2a)/(2 lambda)^(4a+1), and the left Haar factor is dt dy/t^2; Gamma(2a+1)/Gamma(2a)=2a gives the stated constant. The change y=lambda(1+t)z including its Jacobian factorizes the joint density as beta-prime(2a,2a+1) times the normalized symmetric Student-type factor. The beta integrals for (1+T)^q and |Z|^q and Gamma duplication give the stated moments, including mass one at q=0. The first factor has moment threshold 2a+1, with logarithmic divergence at equality, and the independent second has threshold 4a+1; nonnegative integration rules out cancellation. With R=|y| and u=lambda t/R the rescaled marginal integral has kernel u^(2a-1)/[1+(u+lambda/R)^2]^(2a+1). It is bounded by its integrable pointwise limit of mass B(a,a+1)/2, giving both the coefficient and L1 convergence of the normalized conditional densities, hence TV. Gamma log variances give the log-scale result; symmetry and q=2 give the time variance. 'Necessarily' denotes conditional order in probability (the limit is positive, finite and nondegenerate), not a deterministic lower bound on T at a given y. value.rationale: Analytic Cauchy windows are a natural uncertainty model. The scale and time log/ordinary variances have different finiteness regimes; for every real order the exact moment frontier says when the ambiguity-based time statistic can be used. Beyond computing a known kernel, the TV limit quantifies which dilations accompany extreme displacements and gives a usable conditional law, with a sharp tail coefficient for normalization. This is a narrow explicit family calculation, not a general uncertainty-minimization result.
